doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: A couple of months with John Kirby's band
summary: Jones briefly played in Kirby's small band, praising Charlie Shavers's writing and the band's big sound.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: What about your time with John Kirby?

Interesting, because he had Bill Beason, Buster Bailey. That took Billy Cobham’s place for a while. I was overtime. I played with the band sure maybe a couple of months. But Charlie Shavers used to do a lot of the writing for the band. Of course, you know Charlie, he kept playing higher, and higher, and higher. Ease to play the highest notes on the horn. He was a good player. He was a good arranger. He was a very good arrangement and I enjoyed the band. Kirby used to be the bass player with Fletcher Henderson’s band. In fact, when Fletcher Anderson first came to New York Kirby was his bass player. He called his band, "The best little band in the world." He was almost right because the little band had a big sound. Fee arrangements were already really good, very well rehearsed, and the bandages had a really great sound. I enjoyed it.
